## Small module and exact behavior

Add a small PRIVATE bank-egress helper in economy.cpp (or an internal header
within this candidate if necessary for a real production fixture). Its interface
takes intended bank goal tiles, existing TurnBudget and Memory, and returns an
existing RouteStatus. Keep implementation details local; no general navigation
framework or edits to ordinary move_to/retreat/observation behavior.

Call it only inside bank's actual no_route_now/invalid_goals approach branch,
after the original three-failure cooldown/altar-clear operation. Use the local
altar coordinate captured BEFORE any reset, not w.altars[m.altar] after it can
become -1. Require current refreshed camp_hit and positive incoming, current
budget and fuel>reserve. Bank still returnsfalse regardless of egress result.
No invocation on moved/at_goal/wait/deferred, emptybag, noaltar or channels.

Helper contract:

1. Guard current/alive/channel/can-move and existing movement restrictions through
   normal helpers. Snapshot must be current. Use existing budget.admit (30k,
   maxfields3); refuse safely when no field remains. Do not reset field counters.
2. Construct blocked=s.blocked|s.risk, clear self tile, and mask the supplied
   altar goals against it. Do NOT add awake-camp attack regions to this egress
   field. This exception is private to the current failed-bank/camp-hit path.
   Emptygoals->invalid_goals; alreadyatgoal->at_goal, with no new action.
3. Spend at most ONE additional distance field toward these goals, using existing
   SDK distance_field behavior/compute_to and current-round guards. Unreachable
   origin->no_route_now. Do not calculate a route toward spawn or another altar.
4. Enumerate at most8 physically reachable adjacent walking tiles under this
   blocked mask, excluding self. Require finite, STRICTLY LOWER goal distance
   than origin and estimated incoming <= current position. Preserve all existing
   enemy-risk exclusions even if they prevent egress. No dash or diagonal rule
   invented beyond the existing bitboard walking convention.
5. Estimate incoming with EXACT existing incoming_at semantics: visible enemy
   strength inside attack_range, plus visible living awake positive-strength
   camps inside attack_range, Chebyshev. For bounded cost, snapshot these local
   source positions/ranges/strengths ONCE within this helper and evaluate neighbors
   in ordinary C++; retain enemy-then-camp order. Do not add global observation
   caches. Evaluate current-position incoming from this SAME captured threat set
   and accumulation order as neighbors; do not compare different snapshot epochs.
   Do not change existing scans. Check round/fuel during collection; return
   deferred before mutation if an epoch changes or reserve is reached. This local
   copying is implementation cost control, not a new damage model or free work.
6. Among admissible neighbors choose deterministically by (lower goal distance,
   lower incoming,y,x). If none,returnno_route_now WITHOUT increasing blocked a
   second time. The original failed approach already counted its failure.
7. Immediately before one move_checked attempt, recheck current/fuel and existing
   movement availability. On actual move only, resetblocked=0 and setlast_distance
   to the chosen field distance; returnmoved. No success if hidden occupancy
   rejects it, no second retry, bank channel, recall, attack or state mutation.
   Preserve move_checked's observation invalidation and rejection behavior.

Do not claim per-call guards make a whole host query sequence atomic across fuel
suspension. Preserve/extend guards specifically around this new path and document
remaining limitations. The ordinary safe bank route gets first refusal nextturn;
this helper's trigger disappears once camp_hit isfalse. A later safe-to-unsafe
step is not enabled by this fallback when incoming iszero.

Only this failure action changes. Preserve draft/roster, shopping, camp selection,
task lifetime, bankage/bag/endgame rules, queue/courtesy, prior survival/channel
priorities, cooldown/reset order, ordinary navigation, telemetry and coordination.
